name: Madukayang Kalinga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Madukayang Kalinga (madu1248, kmd) is not in the catalog. Both title-works with stress in the title (Edwards et al. 2002 on schizophrenia; Grossman et al. 2010 on autism) are Glottolog false hits: their records read 'Madukayang Kalinga [kmd] (computerized assignment from "affective")'; they are clinical-psychology papers with no bearing on any Kalinga variety (priority none). The language has no published phonological description: the complete OLAC/SIL set for kmd is four survey word lists, Gieser 1958 (mis-filed; it describes Guinaang/Lubuagan Kalinga and says stress is phonemic but 'not fully studied'), the 2012 orthography fact sheets (no Majukayang sheet) and Pittman 1968 (a b/pp/py allophony exercise). The best first-hand evidence read is Gieser's 1973 Madukayang word list, where every polysyllable carries an acute accent on the ultima or penult with no conditioning visible, i.e. lexically contrastive Philippine-type stress; there is no prose placement rule for this variety anywhere I could open. Himes 1997 'Reconstructions in Kalinga-Itneg' (OL 36:1, DOI 10.2307/3623072) remains unread (JSTOR blocked, S2 CLOSED) and is the one medium-priority acquisition; Baguingan 1985 (SLU Baguio PhD) could not be located (S2 0 hits).org and JSTOR 403, web.archive.org unreachable.

new_statements.translation: (word list; glosses are on the English master list, not on this page)
new_statements.citation: Gieser, C. Richard. 1973 (22 Feb). Madukayang Kalinga word list (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List), Amurok, Madukayang, Mountain Province; informants Camilo Diawan & Rosalin Winta. SIL Philippines survey typescript, SIL Language & Culture Archives.
new_statements.locator: pp. 3-4, items 1-88 (stress marked by acute accent); notes page p. 2 has no stress paragraph
new_statements.reading: This is the only first-hand stress evidence for Madukayang itself and it is marked data, not a prose rule: the compiler writes an acute accent on every polysyllable, and the accent sits on either the final syllable (manúk, anák, ugsá, natóy, ngilú, sikorán) or the penult (ámin, ósing, áping, kápos, áso, lúta) with no visible segmental conditioning. Read as lexically contrastive stress confined to the last two syllables, i.e. the ordinary Philippine (Cordilleran) pattern. The companion Saliok list (Shetler & Gieser 1973, note 8) says only 'Single quote (') represents stress'. The one prose statement held by the project, Gieser 1958 §3.3 ('The suprasegmental phonemic contrast is in stress.. Stress has not been fully studied as yet'), describes Guinaang = Lubuagan Kalinga, a different variety already in the catalog.
new_statements.found_by: works with stress in the title

sources.citation: Gieser, C. Richard. 1973 (22 Feb). Madukayang Kalinga word list (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items), given by Camilo Diawan & Rosalin Winta, Amurok, Madukayang, Mountain Province. SIL Philippines unpublished survey typescript.
sources.quote: [p.3, items with acute accent as typed:] magayúd, ámin, sánga, tiklíng, súngbat, dapúr, lawwíng, óppak, man-amós, lawód, múma, títit, úros, sap-úyan, long-ág, ótok, súsu, sikorán, koráppoy; [p.4:] luwáng, ósing, áping, manúk, anák, parátang, kumaráb, súgud, kápos, ugsá, natóy, áso, in-inóp, ammagá, ngilú, lúta, lúnig
sources.locator: p. 2 (NOTES: Glottal, /b/, /d/, [r], Vowels, Grammar) and pp. 3-4 (items 1-88)
sources.note: No prose statement on stress placement anywhere on the notes page (it treats only glottal stop, /b/, /d/, [r], unanalysed vowels and the subject-focus prefix). But every polysyllabic entry carries an acute accent, and the accent falls on the ultima (magayúd, manúk, anák, ugsá, natóy, ngilú, sikorán) or the penult (ámin, sánga, ósing, áping, kápos, áso, lúta) with no phonological conditioning visible: lexically distributed stress of the Philippine type, on one of the last two syllables. This is data, not a rule statement.

sources.note: Only a transcription convention: stress is marked, hence treated as lexically specified; no placement rule given. SIL files this list under Majukayang Kalinga [kmd].

sources.note: The Kalinga exercise is about b / pp / py allophony; stress is not marked in its data and not discussed. Variety unspecified (Gieser's fieldwork was Guinaang/Lubuagan).
